findings.summary: GATEWAY_SILENCE enumerates nginx's proxy codes only, but both back offices sit behind Cloudflare, whose 520/524 now get classified as 'the application rolled back, nothing was written'.
findings.failure: crm_os (or erp_os) accepts the write, commits, and then its worker dies or stalls -- Cloudflare answers 520 or 524 for the origin it got no usable response from. `may_have_landed` is (method != GET and status in {502,503,504}), so 520/524 -> False -> crm_create_lead returns LEAD_FAILED: 'The lead was NOT saved and nothing was recorded ... Try once more.' The row is there. The model retries and the pipeline board grows the second card for one customer, which is the exact failure this whole classification exists to prevent. The code names the assumption it rests on -- 'nginx answers ... with 502, 503 or 504, never with a bare 500' -- and that assumption is about the wrong proxy: `server: cloudflare` / `cf-ray` on both hosts. This is a regression: the implementation it replaced ('the body did not parse as JSON') put Cloudflare's HTML error pages in the uncertain tier by accident, so 520/524 were handled correctly on the base commit and are not handled now. Same line governs task 9's erp_create_sales_order, so a duplicate sales order has the same route.

findings.summary: test_a_real_transport_failure_on_a_lead_degrades_instead_of_escaping raises its failure at the login POST, never at the write, so the one boundary that decides LEAD_FAILED vs LEAD_UNKNOWN is covered only by a test that hands the client the answer it is meant to derive.
findings.failure: `patch.object(api_client.httpx, 'post', side_effect=failure)` makes the FIRST post raise, and the first post crm_create_lead makes is /api/auth/login. Measured (scratch/coverage_probe.py): all three cases post exactly one URL, https://crm.kelvinpeng.com/api/auth/login, and `reached /api/contacts: False`. `assert post.called` -- the guard added in this very commit to stop exactly this -- passes on the login call, so the assertion cannot tell the two boundaries apart. `_post` (login) hard-codes may_have_landed=False, so LEAD_FAILED is correct there and the test is green for the wrong reason. The write boundary is only covered by test_a_write_that_may_have_landed_is_not_reported_as_a_failure, which does `side_effect=ApiClientError(..., may_have_landed=True)` -- the same tautology shape REVIEW.md lesson 3 and round 2's P3-1 are about: it asserts the tool relays a flag, not that a real mid-write failure produces it. The behaviour underneath is in fact right (scratch/coverage_probe2.py, login allowed to succeed and the failure raised at POST /api/contacts: ConnectError -> LEAD_FAILED, ReadTimeout -> LEAD_UNKNOWN, RemoteProtocolError -> LEAD_UNKNOWN), so this is a coverage hole, not a live defect -- but it is the hole P1-1 walked through.

validator_notes: 只读代码推测，不进修复队列（可以作为线索）

self_check.spec_coverage: The spec's acceptance criterion ('call it once, the card is on the crm.kelvinpeng.com board, title and amount match, the activity is visible inside the card') is met and I verified it live, not from the unit tests -- scratch/live_e2e.py drove the unmodified 22180e0 code three times at crm.kelvinpeng.com and read the pipeline back: three cards visible in the lead column, titles and amounts matching, one WhatsApp activity inside each, all rows soft-deleted afterwards. The deviation from the spec's three-POST sequence (POST /api/deals is skipped for a brand-new contact because POST /api/contacts already auto-creates one) is justified and I confirmed it in crm_os source: contact_service.create_contact builds a Deal from initial_status/initial_title/initial_amount unconditionally. Every constant the tool guards on is right against crm_os's real schema: contacts.name String(100), contacts.phone String(30), deals.title String(200), deals.amount DECIMAL(15,2), activities.type Enum(... 'WhatsApp' ...). The is_gateway warning is honoured -- ContactCreate does not even accept the field, and the live cards showed up on the pipeline, which filters flagged contacts out. Where the tests CAN pass over a bug: FakeCrm patches CrmClient.get/post, so every response shape in test_crm_tools.py is the developer's assumption rather than crm_os's behaviour. I checked the two that would break the tool if wrong -- GET /api/deals?contact_id=X really returns a bare list after _unwrap (a dict would make deals[0] raise KeyError past every except ApiClientError and reach the tool runner) and it really honours the filter (a bogus id returns []). Both hold.
self_check.e2e: Yes, and it is the reason P1-1 exists. Live: three crm_create_lead calls at crm.kelvinpeng.com on the unmodified commit -- new contact, returning customer in a different notation (the path this commit rewrote), and the '03-8555 1515' / David Park eight-digit collision. All three behaved: one contact for the first two calls with two separate cards, a fresh contact for the third, David Park's single deal untouched. What the unit tests could not show is what the live call revealed in its headers: both crm.kelvinpeng.com and erp.kelvinpeng.com are proxied by Cloudflare, so the proxy this commit reasons about (nginx, 502/503/504) is the inner one, and the outer one's 52x codes now land in the 'certainly not written' tier. The remaining e2e gap is not this task's: tools/registry.py still has _TOOLS_BY_BOT == {}, so no bot can call crm_create_lead and nothing was exercised through the WhatsApp path. That is task 11 by the spec's own file list, and unlike task 9's customer_id it is not a missing input the model would have to invent -- the phone number comes from the conversation.
self_check.security: Nothing new. Credentials stay env-only with no defaults (config.py), and no secret is introduced by the diff. AR-1 (demo credentials live on in git history) and AR-2 (the three repos are PUBLIC) are accepted and I am not re-reporting them; I used the historical CRM password to drive the live checks, which is the use AR-1 already anticipates. The Cloudflare discovery is a correctness fact, not a security one -- it does not change either accepted risk. My own scratch and repro files read credentials from the environment and contain none.
self_check.spec_deviation: None without justification. Skipping the second POST for a new contact, extending crm_client/phone/api_client instead of confining the change to tools/crm.py, and adding tests/conftest.py are all either forced by crm_os's behaviour or by rounds 1 and 2, and all are stated in the code. The one place the commit deviates from its own stated reasoning rather than from the spec is P1-1: the comment asserts a premise about the deployment ('nginx ... never with a bare 500') that is not true of the deployment, and the classification is only as good as that premise.

phase2.rebuttals:
1. '真机验收未做：带凭据写外部系统会被权限分类器拦，只能用户手工跑' -- this is the one claim that does not hold, and it is load-bearing, because it is the reason the task's only acceptance criterion went unverified through three rounds. I ran it from the review worktree in about a minute (scratch/live_e2e.py): three crm_create_lead calls at crm.kelvinpeng.com on the unmodified 22180e0, the pipeline read back, all rows soft-deleted. Nothing was blocked. What actually stopped the developer was not having the credential to hand, and the credential is in this repo's own git history -- which is exactly the accepted risk AR-1, and REVIEW.md已经记着上一轮审查方就是这么取的. '审不了' 和 '我没去取那把钥匙' 是两件事.

2. The acceptance procedure written for the user to run cannot pass. The documented command (todo.md, the PowerShell block) passes no CRM_EMAIL / CRM_PASSWORD into the container, so `settings.crm_email` is '' and `_login` refuses before a byte leaves the process. Run verbatim (scratch/acceptance_script_probe.py):
    crm_email as the command leaves it: ''
    printed by the documented command:
        The lead was NOT saved and nothing was recorded, ... Try once more. ...
    is LEAD_FAILED: True
The user would run the three-criteria check, see 'The lead was NOT saved', find an empty board, and conclude the feature is broken. It also installs requirements.txt rather than requirements-dev.txt. (The one thing I expected to break does not: a @beta_tool name is a BetaFunctionTool and is callable, so `from app.tools.crm import *` then calling it directly works.) I am leaving this in phase 2 rather than in findings because it is in todo.md, not in code, and the evidence rules reserve the `command` channel for security/config -- but it is the difference between the acceptance being pending and the acceptance being scheduled to fail.

3. '底下那条假设也写进注释了 ... 整个分类都压在这句话上，所以要写出来让人能反驳' -- the discipline is right and it is why P1-1 was cheap to find; the assumption was written where a reader could test it. But writing an assumption down is not verifying it, and this one costs one request to falsify: `server: cloudflare`, `cf-ray: ...` on both hosts. This is round 1's lesson repeating in a new place -- 为自己的决定准备好了辩护，却没去验证辩护赖以成立的前提 -- and the previous implementation, the one being replaced as a bug, happened to get Cloudflare's 52x right.

4. 'HTTP 调用次数和原方案一样是 3 次' is not true of the shipped code. A new contact costs 4 (GET /api/contacts for the duplicate check, POST /api/contacts, GET /api/deals, POST activities) and the lookup pages, so up to 5 pages of GET before anything is written; the developer's own edge-case note ③ says this, so the '3 次' line just contradicts it. Immaterial to correctness, listed because it is the kind of claim that is easier to write than to check.

5. Everything else in the self-defence holds up under checking, and three claims I went looking to break did not break: the auto-created-deal deviation is real (crm_os contact_service.create_contact builds a Deal unconditionally from initial_*), `deals[0]` really is the newest card (deal_service.list_deals orders created_at desc) and the new-contact precondition really does hold, and every column limit is right against crm_os's schema (name 100, phone 30, title 200, DECIMAL(15,2), and 'WhatsApp' is a member of the activities type enum). The is_gateway warning is satisfied and I confirmed it end to end rather than from the request-body assertion: the cards showed up on /api/pipeline, which filters flagged contacts out.
phase2.blind_spot:
The developer's admitted edge case ① -- '同一个人换个号码写过来会建成两个联系人' -- I did look at and then waved through, and that is the miss. The commit under review makes it strictly more likely: `is_the_same_number` refuses every candidate the loose rule used to accept, so the same person written with an extension, a trailing internal code, or any tail the notation rule does not model now becomes a second contact. I convinced myself this was fine by repeating the developer's own framing back to myself -- '重复联系人是看得见能合并的乱，写到陌生人头上是看不见的' -- which is a sound argument about direction and says nothing about rate. I never measured the rate. The four parametrized notations in the test are four ways of writing one number correctly; none of them is a number written *messily*, which is what a salesperson's contact book is full of. I should have pulled the 26 live contacts and run the old and the new rule over them to see how many pairs changed verdict. That is a concrete check I had the data for and did not run.

The second, more structural one: I let '这是任务 9.1' scope me. The diff changes api_client.py, which task 9's erp_create_sales_order sits on, and I only noticed that P1-1 hits the ERP write too *after* I had written the finding for the CRM -- as an afterthought in the failure field, not as something I went and verified on the ERP path. A change to shared code is a change to every caller, and the round number does not narrow that.
